chunks: Habib ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The thief of the dead is cut, just as the thief of the living is cut.'

key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: Is cut (referring to the amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for stealing from a grave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Abu al-Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) from Imam Ali, establishes the principle of *qisas* and *hadd* parity between the living and the dead regarding property rights. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the grave is a repository of the deceased's wealth, thereby extending the standard theft penalty of cutting the hand to grave robbers. This ruling underscores the continuity of personal property rights after death, a key concept in Shia inheritance and penal jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Habeen Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Amro Bin Sabit, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The thief of the dead would be cut just as the thief of the living is cut’.
